subject.title: [Feature]: Batch WhatsApp messages by messageTimestamp instead of receive time

question: Should OpenClaw add a WhatsApp-specific timestamp coalescing mode that intentionally waits beyond the ordinary receive-time debounce window for equal server-timestamp messages?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the grace duration, whether equal second-resolution timestamps may be combined, and whether users need an opt-in setting changes latency and message-turn semantics for a bundled channel.

options.title: Approve a narrow opt-in WhatsApp mode
options.body: Define a bounded grace window and exact account/conversation/sender/timestamp eligibility, then implement it in the WhatsApp extension with live Baileys evidence.

options.title: Keep receive-time debounce only
options.body: Retain the current latency-first behavior and document that delayed WhatsApp delivery cannot be reconstructed safely from second-resolution timestamps.

options.title: Reopen cross-channel coalescing design
options.body: Treat this as input to a new scoped successor of the closed general coalescing RFC if maintainers want a shared scheduling contract across channels.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow opt-in WhatsApp mode
recommendation.body: Define a bounded grace window and exact account/conversation/sender/timestamp eligibility, then implement it in the WhatsApp extension with live Baileys evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent WhatsApp monitor ownership and the existing issue review make steipete the strongest available routing candidate for the behavioral contract.
